verdict.rationale: The only relevant evidence is a Kimi help-center category that lists memory (记忆) among the general features. That suggests the product itself offers some persistent context, but nothing shows user-set custom instructions or preferences, or that they shape every response. missing for 10: documented custom-instructions/preferences settings, evidence that stored preferences apply across all responses, user-editable memory controls, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can set persistent custom instructions and preferences that shape every response
